rules.statement: When a background loop acquires a resource (such as a session or lease) and cancellation can interrupt it before the resource is published to the field that shutdown cleans up, keep the acquired-but-unpublished resource tracked and release it on stop, using a token other than the one that was cancelled.
rules.why: Otherwise a stop during the follow-up step leaks the resource until it expires, skipping a graceful release and blocking a restarted node from reclaiming it.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks filtered on `!stopping.IsCancellationRequested` or similar that let cancellation escape after an acquire but before the resource is assigned to the state the stop path releases.

rules.statement: Validate options that become `PeriodicTimer` or timer periods against a minimum of one millisecond, using a shared named minimum constant, and name the option's configuration key in each failure message.
rules.why: `PeriodicTimer` throws for periods under 1 ms, so a value that only passes an above-zero check fails later at run time instead of at start-time validation.
rules.check: Look for TimeSpan options validated only as `> TimeSpan.Zero` that feed a `PeriodicTimer`, `Task.Delay` or timer, and failure messages that don't name the option.

rules.statement: Test every point at which a background loop can be stopped, including stopping during a retry or back-off wait, and assert that the stop completes, the final state is stopped, and no more work runs.
rules.why: If cancellation of a wait were mishandled, the host would hang in stop or log a spurious failure, and no test would catch it.
rules.check: For each awaited delay or wait in a hosted loop, look for a test that stops the host while the loop waits there without advancing the fake clock.

rules.statement: When code tolerates a transient failure and keeps retrying, add a test where one attempt fails and the next succeeds, and assert that the state degrades and then recovers.
rules.why: A regression that gave up after one failure would otherwise pass the suite, and a brief outage would drop the resource.
rules.check: For retry or renew loops, look for a test with a failure followed by a success, not only tests that fail until the deadline.

rules.statement: Test validation bounds at the exact limit and one step past it on each side, and assert that the failure names the property.
rules.why: Flipping `>=` and `>`, or `<` and `<=`, would otherwise pass every test even though the bounds are specified exactly.
rules.check: For range validation, look for tests that only use values far past each limit and have no cases at the limit and one tick or unit outside it.

rules.statement: In tests of failure paths that log, pass a `FakeLogger<T>` from `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.Testing` instead of `NullLogger` and assert the event id and level of the expected entry.
rules.why: Operators rely on these entries to see why a node isn't ready, and a dropped, mislevelled or renumbered entry would otherwise fail no test.
rules.check: Look for fault-path tests that use only `NullLogger` and never assert a log record for the error or warning the path writes.

rules.statement: Make XML documentation state the behaviour the code actually has: if a callback that throws is caught and logged, the remarks must say so instead of saying callbacks must not throw.
rules.why: A documented contract that disagrees with the behaviour, and with the tests that pin it, misleads callers.
rules.check: Compare `<remarks>` and summaries that forbid or promise something against the implementation's catch blocks and the tests.

rules.statement: Replace a string literal that is repeated in several places in a type with one private const.
rules.check: Look for the same string literal written inline more than once in a class.

rules.statement: In tests that check an exception message, assert the exact message or its full distinctive text, not a short substring.
rules.why: A different failure that happens to mention the substring would still pass, so the test doesn't prove the intended check failed.
rules.check: Look for `Assert.Contains("<fragment>", exception.Message)` where the message is deterministic and could be asserted exactly.

rules.statement: Don't ask to replace a synchronous `CancellationTokenSource.Cancel()` with `await CancelAsync()` when its callbacks must finish before the next step, unless a convention requires `CancelAsync`.
rules.why: Awaiting `CancelAsync()` also waits for every callback, so it doesn't stop a slow callback from delaying the next step, and the ordering is deliberate.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the code relies on callbacks finishing before it continues, and whether the repository's conventions actually require `CancelAsync`.

rules.statement: Don't ask for `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on a source-generated logging class unless the repository's conventions require it.
rules.why: The conventions describe the logging class without the attribute, and the coverage gate passes with the class counted.
rules.check: Before reporting, check the logging section of the conventions and whether any sibling project uses the attribute.

rules.statement: Don't report `params IEnumerable<T>` or other params collection parameters as unable to bind individual arguments when the projects build with C# 13 or later.
rules.why: C# 13 params collections accept individual element arguments, and the shared project template sets the latest language version.
rules.check: Before reporting, check the LangVersion that the build props set.

rules.statement: Don't ask for `IServiceCollection` parameters, extension receivers or locals to be renamed from `services` unless the repository's conventions state such a naming rule.
rules.why: No convention requires it, and the sibling registration code uses `services`.
rules.check: Before reporting, check the C# conventions file and how the sibling service-collection extensions name the receiver.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask to replace a private nested `FakeTimeProvider` subclass that overrides one member, such as `CreateTimer` to throw, with a strict `Mock<TimeProvider>`.
rules.why: The test conventions allow a stub one test file needs as a `private sealed` nested type, and the subclass still uses `FakeTimeProvider` as the time convention asks while changing only the behaviour under test.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the stub derives from `FakeTimeProvider`, is nested in the one test file that uses it, and overrides only what the test needs.

rules.statement: Don't ask for an event-id `Base` constant to be made private when its containing class is already `internal`, unless the conventions require it.
rules.why: The logging convention only asks for named event-id constants written as `Base + n`, and an internal class already limits `Base` to the assembly.
rules.check: Before reporting, check the accessibility of the containing class and what the logging convention actually requires.

rules.statement: Wrap Markdown paragraphs and list items in decision records to fill lines to about 120 columns, without short lines in the middle of a paragraph, except before a link too long to share a line.
rules.why: Wrap checks and formatters flag uneven paragraphs.
rules.check: Look for lines that end well short of 120 columns while the sentence continues on the next line.
